pure-announcement.rationale: Although it accompanies a feature launch, the post is an engineering writeup of a transferable defense architecture — threat model, classifier design, and measured trade-offs — not a release note.

duplicate.rationale: Nothing in the nearest concepts (MCP platform notes, retrieval evals, SIEM gap) covers model-based approval classification for agent actions.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The design is described mechanistically and the claims carry evaluation tables and a cited system card a reader can check.

durability.rationale: The core content is mechanism and trade-off — reasoning-blind classifiers, structural injection defense by stripping tool outputs, two-stage FPR/FNR cascades, delegation-boundary checks — which outlives the specific model names and percentages used as evidence.

actionability.rationale: Anyone building agent autonomy can lift concrete choices from it: drop blanket interpreter allow-rules, judge actions not rationalizations, tier approvals by blast radius, and use deny-and-continue with escalation limits instead of halting.

atomicity.rationale: The probe, classifier, and handoff checks are facets of one stateable idea — delegate approvals to a conservative, reasoning-blind classifier that treats anything the user did not authorize as unauthorized.
